name: Make several video ad versions from one product photo, with the price shown first (MartLLM)

parameters.formTitle: Make video ads from a product photo
parameters.formDescription: Upload one clear photo of your product and say what the ads should get across. You see the price of every version before anything is made.

values.placeholder: e.g. Light, breathable, machine washable. For busy commuters. Casual and honest.

assignments.name: script_instructions
assignments.value:
You write short UGC-style video ads for online stores. You get one product photo, the product name, what the ads should say, how many versions to write, the video length and whether the videos have a voice.

Write that many versions of the ad. Each version takes a clearly different angle (for example: the problem it solves, a first try, a day in use, a close look at the details, a quick honest review), with a different place and a different opening.

The photo becomes the first frame of every video. Each video must start from exactly what is in the photo and keep the product looking the same the whole time: same shape, colors, label and printed text.

Each version is ONE continuous shot that a phone could film: a real person (a creator) showing or using the product in an everyday place, natural light, handheld feel. Say what the camera does, what the person does and where they are, in plain concrete words. Keep it to what can happen in the video length.

Never add on-screen text, logos, prices, discounts or claims that are not in the brief. Never promise health or medical results.

If the videos have a voice, the person says one short line out loud that fits the video length (about 2.5 words per second). Put it in the video_prompt in quotes, after 'says:'. If there is no voice, spoken_line is an empty string.

Answer with JSON only: {"versions": [{"angle": "the angle in a few words", "video_prompt": "...", "spoken_line": "...", "caption": "a caption for the post, at most 125 characters"}]}

parameters.content:
## Several video ads from one product photo

Upload a product photo and a short brief, and choose 2 to 5 versions. A model looks at the photo and writes each version from a different angle. You then see the price of every version and the total, and choose whether to go on. The videos are made at the same time and download as one zip file.

### Set up (2 minutes)
1. Get an API key at [martllm.com](https://martllm.com/go/n8n-ad-video-variants) and add credit.
2. Open **Save the photo** → Credential → Create new → **Header Auth**:
   - Name: `Authorization`
   - Value: `Bearer ` followed by your key
   Every MartLLM step uses this one credential.
3. Turn the workflow on, open **Product form** and copy its link. Share the link with anyone on your team who needs ads.

### What it costs
You always see the real price before anything is made. On 2026-11-25 the price list showed $0.085 per second at 720p and $0.039 per second at 480p for the default model, so three 5 second versions at 720p were about $1.27. Writing the versions costs a fraction of a cent. A video that is not made costs nothing. Live prices: [martllm.com/models](https://martllm.com/models?type=video).

### Change it here
**Settings** holds the video model with a backup, 480p or 720p, the writing model, the most one video may cost, and the writing rules (tone, what never to say).

The videos take the shape of your photo: upload a tall photo for a tall video.

### The price comes first
**Price each version** asks MartLLM what each exact video costs. Nothing is made and nothing is charged for asking. **Show the price** puts the list on the form page and waits for your answer. If MartLLM refuses a request, the form shows MartLLM's own message and nothing starts.

### All versions at once
Every version starts at the same time, so three videos take about as long as one: usually 1 to 5 minutes. The workflow checks every 20 seconds and stops waiting after 15 minutes. If one version is not made, the others still come through and the last page says which one failed and why.

### Where the videos go
They download as one zip file on the form page. To keep every video, put a Google Drive, Slack or S3 step after **Download each video**: each file is in the `video` field. MartLLM keeps the files for about 3 hours.
